prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Input: Sole edit target is the original full Silent Storm character clothing diffuse UV atlas, enlarged exactly4x nearest-neighbor only to reveal original tiny forms.
Request: Faithful HD reconstruction of original surface detail. Return only the same complete square 1:1 flat opaque atlas. No garment render, scene or redesign.
Source material, layout and exact inventory: Left very dark brown trouser panel, right upper muted dark blue folded cloth panel with exactly ONE thin horizontal dark red stripe at its original height (original y35). Bottom-right worn near-black leather boot/accessory island and rounded upper projection. Preserve dark color contrast, original folds and black gaps; do not add more stripes.
UV lock: Every original island, seam, shadow, fold, marking and black cutout stays at its exact normalized original coordinates, shape, count and size. No crop, margin, zoom, rotation, repacking, bounding-box registration or altered patch scale. Preserve all original materials and opaque black gaps.
Fine surface detail: Only subtle random wool/canvas fiber grain and fine worn leather within existing forms. Plain cloth stays plain, no jacquard, diamond print or ornamental pattern. Preserve the scale and frequency of existing stripes, ribs, dots, lacing and repeated detail. Retain original muted color and dark exposure; numerical brightness correction later.
Do not invent anything: No new pockets, belts, straps, stitches, buttons, holes, eyelets, metal parts, rivets, zippers, damage, symbols, logos, letters, insignia or objects. Never turn an ambiguous low-contrast mark into new recognisable hardware or glyph. Keep tiny original markings faint and their original exact forms.
provenance_recovered: Raw SHA-256 exactly matches retained built-in output in original clothing agent folder. Existing canonical exact prompt retained; no new generation call.
reference_recipe: Original full canvas enlarged exactly4x nearest-neighbor only for generation reference; no crop/bbox/UV or RGB restoration.
